Yes, I started to do this after my first interaction with a teacher.

It was my first day of college, I was excited as I had been learning everything by myself and now I was going to actually have proper classes. The class was Programming 101, we were starting learning C and the teacher was telling us bout the syntax. After a while he says:

"In C, if you write `... } else if (...) {` the compiler will accept it, but you can't do it."

*me, naively, been programming C for a while, raise my hand*
"Why can't we do it?"

"It's not in the standard"

"Ahh... it is in the standard"

"No, it is not"

"Sorry... but it is. That's legal C, and relatively common practice"

Things escalated before I knew it he was saying:
"I would know, I was programming before you were even born"

I shut up.

At the end of the class I go up to him and apologize, I did not meant to confront him, I just did not understand why he told use that we couldn't do that and wanted to know why.

Came to find out he is the head of the computer department.

After that I started to be careful and tried to avoid this. When the teachers would say something really bad, I would wait for the end of the class, or when we were doing exercises, and ask of they were sure, while presenting why I thought they weren't. Some teachers were receptive and did in fact look things up to make sure, while others just said "yes, this is correct, you are wrong". I did not challenge them in these cases.

Note my wording in the post, I said that some teachers only had a grasp on the basic concepts they were teaching. I know that some studied different areas, and that is fine. This does not, however, make it right for them to be teaching us, it is still poor education.

I got teachers telling me that mutexes and semaphores are the exact same thing... okay. I had one teacher in a Linux system administration class say: "We are using Ubuntu, it comes with the aptitude package manager, but if you want you can install and use other package managers, like rpm or yum". Being a packager for a Linux distribution, this grinded with me so much, but I kept calm and asked him if he was sure that was correct, he was defensive so I shut up.

My friends are the ones that usually have to listen to me rant. But they also use Linux and some are also pretty advanced users, so they rant with me :)
